title: What is a person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC)?
description: A PRRC is the qualified person an EU medical device maker must name under MDR Article 15. Qualification routes, duties and how it compares with similar roles.
shortAnswer: A person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC) is the named, qualified individual that every medical device manufacturer and authorized representative placing devices on the European Union market must have under Article 15 of the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) and the In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation (IVDR). The PRRC must meet set education and experience routes and is responsible for ensuring release checks, technical documentation, post-market surveillance and vigilance reporting are done.
keyTakeaways: The PRRC is an EU specific role created by Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR), applying since 26 May 2021, and the parallel Article 15 of the IVDR, applying since 26 May 2022.
Qualification is fixed by law: a relevant degree plus at least one year of regulatory or quality management experience with medical devices, or four years of that experience.
Article 15(3) lists five minimum responsibilities, from checking conformity before release to fulfilling vigilance reporting obligations.
MDCG 2019-7 guidance expects the experience to be substantive, recent and related to EU requirements.
Similar named roles exist in other life sciences practices, such as the GDP Responsible Person and the pharmacovigilance QPPV.
alsoKnownAs: designated person responsible for regulatory compliance

blocks.text: A PRRC makes sure a device manufacturer's core regulatory obligations are met before and after devices reach the market. [MDR Article 15(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02017R0745-20261109) says the PRRC "shall at least be responsible for ensuring that":

items: the conformity of the devices is appropriately checked, in accordance with the quality management system, before a device is released;
the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity are drawn up and kept up to date;
the post-market surveillance obligations are complied with in accordance with Article 10(10);
the reporting obligations referred to in Articles 87 to 91 are fulfilled;
for investigational devices, the statement referred to in Section 4.1 of Chapter II of Annex XV is issued.

blocks.text: Article 15(5) protects the role: the PRRC shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization for properly fulfilling their duties.

sections.heading: What qualifications does a PRRC need?

blocks.text: A PRRC qualifies through one of two routes in Article 15(1), or a third route for custom-made devices. Training cannot replace these routes, but it is how a PRRC keeps experience current.

blocks.caption: PRRC qualification routes under MDR Article 15(1) (summary)
head: Route
Formal qualification
Experience
rows: University degree or recognized equivalent in law, medicine, pharmacy, engineering or another relevant scientific discipline
At least one year in regulatory affairs or quality management systems relating to medical devices
Four years in regulatory affairs or quality management systems relating to medical devices
At least two years within a relevant field of manufacturing

blocks.text: The Medical Device Coordination Group's guidance [MDCG 2019-7 Rev.1](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/463b4f08-44a2-4018-9957-488bf386fc3a_en?filename=md_mdcg_2019_7_guidance_art15_mdr_ivdr_en.pdf) (December 2023) adds that experience should be substantive, recent and related to EU requirements, and that administrative document handling and shadowing alone are not sufficient. Micro and small enterprises may have an external PRRC permanently and continuously at their disposal under Article 15(2). The full detail, including employment and location rules, is on [EU MDR PRRC qualification requirements](/regulations/eu-mdr-prrc-qualification-requirements).

sections.heading: How does a PRRC compare with other named roles in life sciences?

blocks.text: The PRRC is one of several roles where life sciences law names an individual and sets their qualifications or training. The table compares four examples across [GxP](/glossary/gxp) practices.

sections.heading: What evidence should a manufacturer keep for its PRRC?

blocks.text: A manufacturer should keep evidence that the PRRC meets a qualification route and keeps their expertise current. MDCG 2019-7 gives examples: the curriculum vitae, copies of relevant certificates and proof of the professional experience, which competent authorities may request under Article 93(3)(b).

items: Degree certificate or equivalence recognition, if using route (a).
Dated employment history showing device regulatory or quality management experience.
A written allocation of responsibilities where several PRRCs share the role (Article 15(4)).
A development record covering MDR or IVDR changes, guidance updates and vigilance practice.
The PRRC's details as registered in EUDAMED under Annex VI, Part A, Section 1.4.

blocks.text: Other staff who support the PRRC, such as those performing release checks or vigilance reporting, need their own competence evidence, usually managed through the quality system's [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents the PRRC's Article 15(3) responsibilities as defined competencies linked to the procedures they verify. Supporting roles are mapped to the same procedures, so when a release or vigilance procedure changes, both the PRRC's development needs and the affected staff assessments are visible.

faqs.q: Is the PRRC the same as the QPPV?
faqs.a: No. The QPPV is responsible for a medicinal product marketing authorization holder's pharmacovigilance system under EU pharmacovigilance law. The PRRC is a medical device role under MDR and IVDR Article 15, covering release checks, technical documentation, post-market surveillance and vigilance reporting for devices.

faqs.q: Does a non-EU manufacturer need a PRRC?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 15 applies to manufacturers placing devices on the EU market wherever they are based. Non-EU manufacturers also appoint an authorized representative, which needs its own PRRC under Article 15(6), and MDCG 2019-7 says the two cannot be the same person.

faqs.q: Can one person be PRRC for several companies?
faqs.a: Generally not for several legal manufacturers within a group, since MDCG 2019-7 expects each legal manufacturer to have its own PRRC. Micro and small enterprises may use an external PRRC under contract, provided the person is permanently and continuously at their disposal.

faqs.q: Does the PRRC need ongoing training?
faqs.a: Article 15 does not set a training requirement or interval. However, MDCG 2019-7 expects experience to be recent and related to EU requirements, so a documented record of updates on MDR or IVDR changes and guidance is the practical way to show expertise remains current.
